small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose kernel has IC=3 inside the innermost loop with redundant divisions per kw — hoist `pd_num//SD`, `ph_num//SH` out of inner loops (already partly done), and unroll the IC loop with `tl.static_range` since IC=3 is tiny. Try BLOCK_OW=64/128 with num_warps=4 and num_stages=2-3.
- Add `@triton.autotune` over BLOCK_OW ∈ {32,64,128}, num_warps ∈ {2,4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3,4} keyed on (N,OC,OD,OH,OW).
- The pool kernel is launched with BLOCK=16 over PW=16 (one block per row) — increase BLOCK to cover an entire (PH,PW) plane per program (e.g. fuse pid_dh tiles) to reduce launch overhead; or use BLOCK=PH*PW=256 with one program per (N,C,PD).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite ConvTranspose3d as a gather-style implicit-GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile) accumulating over GEMM-K = IC*KD*KH*KW. With IC=3, KD=KH=KW=3, K=81 — small enough for a single-tile loop, and OC=16 fits in one BLOCK_N. Use `tl.dot` on (BLOCK_M, 16) × (16-ish) tiles for tensor-core throughput instead of the current scalar accumulate.
- Fuse the AvgPool3d+bias+scale2 epilogue directly into the conv-transpose kernel: have each program emit the 2×2×2 pooled output cell instead of the full transposed-conv volume. This eliminates the 8× intermediate write/read (conv output is ~128·16·31·63·63 ≈ 250M elements) which is the dominant memory cost; the pooled output is 8× smaller. Tile the program over pooled-spatial coordinates and loop the 8 contributing transposed-conv positions internally.
- Alternatively, scatter-add formulation: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing input×weight outer products into a shared output tile via atomic adds — but on this shape gather+pool-fusion is the better fit. Use channels-last (NDHWC) layout for the conv output staging so the OC axis is contiguous for the pool reduction.
